title: Isle of Man
capsule: Between 1344 and 1402 the Isle of Man was in contested English possession following its final capture from Scottish-aligned lords around 1346, having previously passed between the Scottish and English crowns repeatedly since the 1290s. The English Crown granted the island to a succession of magnates as a feudal lordship; by 1399 it had reverted directly to the Crown. The island's indigenous Tynwald continued to exercise legislative functions throughout, making it one of the oldest continuously operating parliaments in the world, even as external sovereignty remained contested.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The island's territorial extent is defined and clear; the uncertainty is in the succession of lords and the precise legal status at any given point in the 1344–1402 window, rather than in geography.
